A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMPO research work. All pages, including the algorithm, theoretical appendices, experimental details, figures, and example outputs, are readable and can be matched despite repagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original DMPO fine-tuning results on four reasoning benchmarks, training-efficiency comparisons, ablations, and generated examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds DMPO-Dream evaluations and further baseline comparisons in Tables 1 and 2.

M1.justification: The WDCE and WDDO objectives, three weight-baseline choices, replay-buffer procedure, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Applying DMPO to Dream does not introduce a documented algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH500, three-number Countdown, 4×4 Sudoku, and the retained s1k SFT setup. The new Dream experiments reuse existing tasks and datasets rather than introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated wd1-LLaDA and GDPO-LLaDA comparisons across all four tasks at generation lengths 256 and 512, retaining d1 and cGRPO. This substantially broadens the RL comparator set; wd1's earlier citation alone was not an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: v3 extends DMPO fine-tuning and evaluation to Dream-Instruct (7B), with its new comparison using generation lengths 256 and 512. The retained LLaDA experiments keep their stated lengths, zero-shot prompting, training budgets, and dataset procedures.

E4.justification: The negative-gradient ablation, sampler and training-efficiency comparisons, rollout-count and buffer-frequency sensitivity analyses, entropy analysis, and two example outputs are retained. The new Dream table supplies benchmark results rather than a separate ablation.

E5.justification: Benchmark tables continue to report point estimates, and the existing shaded training curves are retained. Neither version supplies additional seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or explanations of the shading.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes DMPO-LLaDA Sudoku scores from 24.56 to 63.80 at length 256 and from 19.97 to 56.67 at length 512, substantially changing its ranking. It also adds wd1/GDPO results, while Table 2 adds d1-Dream and DMPO-Dream results. Figure 1 still reports 24.56, leaving the revised Sudoku result internally inconsistent.

T1.justification: The numbered mathematical development and Appendix B's derivations and proofs are unchanged. The expanded SOC sketch in Section 3.2 recapitulates the path-measure construction and WDCE relationship already presented in Appendix B.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution IV replace the headline improvements of 54.3% and 66.41% with 39.63 and 67.97 percentage points, explicitly identifying prior non-DMPO RL baselines. The central distribution-matching and weight-baseline contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4 now interprets the Dream results as evidence of effectiveness across different dLLM backbones. The conclusion updates the limitation from one tested pretrained dLLM to two, while retaining uncertainty about other models and domains.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the implementation library, LoRA configuration, optimizer settings, GPU hardware, training budgets, sampling details, and code/data access information. The added comparisons are not accompanied by distinct new training or baseline-reproduction recipes.

R1.justification: v3 adds the GDPO reference and broadens the comparison framing beyond d1 as the principal SOTA RL baseline. wd1 was already discussed in Appendix A. Several other reference changes update publication metadata rather than introduce different research.

P1.justification: v3 polishes sentences throughout the main text, expands the SOC explanation, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. The section organization and overall narrative remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with substantial reflow and figure relocation. Table 1 gains comparator rows and revised highlighting, and a separate Dream comparison table is added. Appendix displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The Dream experiments and expanded comparator set strengthen empirical breadth, and the headline comparison is more explicitly defined. However, v3's new 39.63-point headline advantage relies on the 63.80 Sudoku score in Table 1, while Figure 1 retains 24.56 under the same stated setting. Neither the main text nor appendices explain the discrepancy. This conflict affects a central performance claim, preventing a reliable judgment that the benefits outweigh the loss of internal consistency.
